observations: Photo 0 shows a black X-style keyboard stand with a power cable hanging from it.
Photo 1 shows a grey electronic keyboard on the stand, with a small LCD screen and control buttons visible.
Photo 2 shows the same keyboard from a side angle, confirming the grey body and the layout of the control panel.
The keyboard has a standard 61-key layout.
The LCD screen in photo 2 appears to be powered on, displaying some text.

claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.
The photos show a standard electronic keyboard, but 'professional' is a subjective marketing term.
Photo 0 shows a power cable and a stand, which typically includes the power adapter.

claims.claim: All keys and buttons working, Bought from the UK, no dead key, no crackle.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not power on or the LCD screen may be broken.
risks.proof: A video of the keyboard being turned on and the screen displaying a menu.

risks.risk: Individual keys or buttons may be unresponsive or 'dead'.
risks.proof: A video of a chromatic scale being played across all keys.

risks.risk: The internal battery may be dead or the battery compartment may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo of the back of the keyboard showing the battery compartment.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a constant power adapter

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the keyboard powered on with the LCD screen active.
Video of a person playing the keyboard to demonstrate all keys and buttons work.
Photo of the back of the keyboard showing the battery compartment.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
